## Intent
Hypothesis: a branchless blend of the death verdict via per-particle hash RNG can suppress branch misprediction and sustain near-streaming bandwidth across all death rates.

## Layout & approach
The AoS layout packs 68 B/particle, but loop 1 touches only 32 bytes (47% hot — age+pos+seed+vel) and loop 2 touches 28 (41% hot — color+pos), leaving 53–59% dead weight per cache line. No intermediate storage keeps the verdict in registers but forces both loops to stride the full 68-byte struct. The blend approach aimed to replace branchy respawn with arithmetic masking. The working set spills from L1d at N≈963 and L2 at N≈61680; the low hot fraction means each spill carries roughly twice the useful bytes.

## Cache saturation
At q=0.01 cost is flat across regimes: 6.7 ns/p at N=380 (L1d), 6.0 at N=1400 (L2), 5.5 at N=100000 (DRAM) — no knee at either spill. The algo is compute-bound (69–80% compute at q=0.01), so memory latency from dead bytes hides behind the scalar hash-RNG chain. The L1d→L2 and L2→DRAM transitions produce no visible step because the `eor`/`mul`/`lsr` RNG dominates cycles, not line fills. Cost gently decreases as N grows, confirming overhead amortization over streaming.

## Bandwidth
The memory floor is 2.274 ns/p; the algo's best is 5.46 ns/p (N=100000, q=0.01), 2.4× the floor — 58% of time is compute/branch overhead. Achieved bandwidth peaks at 12.5 GB/s (42% of the 29.9 ceiling) at q=0.01, collapsing to 6.2 GB/s at q=0.5. Compute-bound at q≤0.01 (69–80% compute), branch-bound by q=0.25 (branch_flush 31–33%), dominated at q=0.5 (41–45%). Against baseline: 0.74–0.93× at q=0.01, narrowing to 0.81–0.83× at q=0.5. Against winner: 1.25× best to 2.04× worst.

## Assembly
The codegen betrays the blend intent: loop 1 retains 7 conditional branches, loop 2 retains 15 — "branchless" did not eliminate them. Only 9 of 319 instructions are vectorized. Loop 1 uses `fmul.4s`/`fadd.4s` for position integration and `ext.16b` for lane shuffling, but the hash RNG is a scalar `eor`/`mul`/`lsr` chain with indexed gather (`ldr s18, [x5, w25, uxtw #2]`). Loop 2 is entirely scalar FP with `csel` ×18 for clamping and `strb` ×17 for byte-granular scatter — these byte stores cannot coalesce, capping bandwidth below ceiling.

## Verdict
Partially refuted — beats naive everywhere (0.74–0.93× baseline) but never approaches the winner (1.25–2.04×) or the streaming ceiling (42% at best). The "branchless" blend left 7+15 conditional branches, so branch_flush rises from 4–8% at q=0.01 to 45% at q=0.5. With only 9/319 vector instructions and byte-granular `strb` scatter in loop 2, the algo cannot stream. The scalar hash-RNG compute keeps it ahead of naive, but the winner's autovec/halide variants exploit the same layout far more effectively.
